title: Norms & Matrix Condition
description: Vector and matrix norms, condition number of a matrix, perturbation theorem for linear systems.
html:
📏 Norms & Matrix Condition

1. Vector Norms

$$\|x\|_1 = \sum|x_i|, \quad \|x\|_2 = \sqrt{\sum x_i^2}, \quad \|x\|_\infty = \max|x_i|$$

Unit balls: rhombus, circle, square. $\|x\|_\infty \le \|x\|_2 \le \|x\|_1 \le \sqrt n\|x\|_2 \le n\|x\|_\infty$ (norm equivalence).

2. Induced Matrix Norms

$$\|A\| = \max_{x\ne0}\frac{\|Ax\|}{\|x\|}, \quad \|A\|_1 = \max_j\sum_i|a_{ij}|, \quad \|A\|_\infty = \max_i\sum_j|a_{ij}|, \quad \|A\|_2 = \sqrt{\lambda_{\max}(A^TA)}$$

$\|Ax\| \le \|A\|\|x\|$, $\|AB\| \le \|A\|\|B\|$. Example $A = \begin{pmatrix}1&2\\3&4\end{pmatrix}$: $\|A\|_1 = 6$, $\|A\|_\infty = 7$, $\|A\|_2 = 5.465$.

3. Condition Number and Perturbation Theorem

$$\mathrm{cond}(A) = \|A\|\|A^{-1}\| \ge 1, \qquad \frac{\|\Delta x\|}{\|x\|} \le \mathrm{cond}(A)\Bigl(\frac{\|\Delta b\|}{\|b\|}\ \text{or}\ \frac{\|\Delta A\|}{\|A\|}\Bigr)$$

Example

$A = \begin{pmatrix}1&1\\1&1.0001\end{pmatrix}$, $b = (2, 2.0001)^T \Rightarrow x = (1,1)^T$; $\tilde b = (2, 2.0002)^T \Rightarrow \tilde x = (0, 2)^T$. $\mathrm{cond}_\infty(A) = 40004$.

Rule of thumb: $\log_{10}\mathrm{cond}(A)$ decimal digits are lost. $\mathrm{cond}_2(Q) = 1$ for orthogonal $Q$; $\mathrm{cond}_2 = \sigma_{\max}/\sigma_{\min}$; $\mathrm{cond}_2(A^TA) = \mathrm{cond}_2(A)^2$.

4. Residual, Scaling, Refinement

  • A small residual $\Rightarrow$ small error only if the condition is small: $\frac{\|x - \tilde x\|}{\|x\|} \le \mathrm{cond}(A)\frac{\|r\|}{\|b\|}$.
  • Scaling/equilibration can drastically reduce the condition.
  • Iterative refinement: $Ad = b - A\tilde x$, $\hat x = \tilde x + d$ (residual in higher precision).

5. Typical Mistakes

  • Mixing up the column-sum and row-sum norms.
  • Taking $\|A\|_2$ as the largest eigenvalue magnitude of $A$ although $A$ is not symmetric (correct: $\sqrt{\lambda_{\max}(A^TA)}$).
  • Using the determinant as a measure for “nearly singular”.
